To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) H4 genes in eukarya evolve according to the "birth-and-death" mode, (2) histones diverged before the eukarya diverged, (3) histone H1, H3, H4 and H2A, and H2B genes form separate clusters, (4) H1, H4, and H2A/H2B genes diverged at the same time.
the histone H3 and H4 genes are subject to birth-and-death evolution under strong purify selection and that these genes diverged from each other before the eukarya diverged.

the histone H1, H3, H2A and H2B gene families evolve under strong purifying and concerted selection, while the histone H3 and H4 gene families are subject to purifying selection and birth and death evolution.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the long-term evolution and the birth-and-death process of the histone gene family.
the long-term evolution and the molecular phylogeny of the H4 histone gene family.
the evolution of a multigene superfamily under strong purifying and positive selection.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
histone gene family evolution in eukaryotic genomes is driven by strong purifying selection and birth and death of genes.
histone genes have evolved under purifying selection and are not subject to concerted evolution.
histone genes in the nucleus have undergone birth-and-death evolution and that concerted evolution does not occur in this gene family.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
histone genes evolved in a manner similar to that of the globin gene family, which also evolves under the birth-and-death mechanism and has a high degree of protein conservation.
histone genes have evolved under strong purifying selective pressure and have undergone birth-and-death evolution.

histone genes in the five classes have evolved independently since the divergence of eukaryotic and archaebacterial lineages, and the high level of sequence homogeneity in histone genes was generated by the strong purifying selection acting upon these genes.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the histone H2B and H3 genes have been evolving under the birth-and-death mode of evolution for a long time, which has resulted in the accumulation of a large number of H2B and/or H3 pseudogenes in the eukaryote genomes.
the high degree of sequence similarity among histone H4 proteins in different species does not necessarily imply that concerted evolution has occurred.
purifying selection is a more powerful force than gene conversion in maintaining sequence homogeneity in histone genes.
